message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on "Desert Atlas" stone. It is an igneous rock with almost no quartz, so it is not granite in the tariff sense, which requires quartz. That points to "other monumental or building stone" in heading 6802. The stone is cut into slabs and polished on one side.

HTS 6802.93 covers granite, worked, and 6802.99 covers other stone. Since the lab found little quartz, the stone is likely not classified as granite under the tariff's definition. CBP generally treats "granite" as including igneous rocks with quartz, but a rock with almost no quartz (such as gabbro or basalt) is classified as "other stone".

Heading 6802 covers monumental or building stone, worked, other than slate. Subheading 6802.91 covers marble, travertine, and alabaster. 6802.92 covers other calcareous stone. 6802.93 covers granite. 6802.99 covers other stone.

Since the stone is not granite, 6802.99 applies. The 6802.99.00 subheading has statistical suffixes: 6802.99.0010 is for "Other: Slabs" if I recall, and 6802.99.0090 is for other. I believe 6802.99.00 has 10 for "Slabs" and 90 for "Other". Because the goods are large slabs, I will use the slab suffix.

Alternatively, the stone could be classified as 2515 or 2516 if merely cut into rectangular blocks or slabs. Because the top is polished, it counts as further worked, so heading 6802 applies.
